searched: coordinator's relayed evidence (372/374-commit full-history scans, redacted JSON report, checksum-mismatch demonstration) — not a file this review can independently read

findings.summary: F-3-1's specific illustrative risk — that the historical 'fake_api_key' finding in test_context_assistant.py's history might be a value .gitleaks.toml's allowlist doesn't cover, producing an un-ignored 17th finding — is resolved by the evidence relayed this round (the coordinator's and builder's full-history `gitleaks git` runs over 372 and 374 commits returning exit 0/no leaks, and a redacted JSON report confirming the value-anchored allowlist reaches it). That part of the original finding no longer stands. What the fix itself adds, however, is only a six-line comment ('Verify BEFORE extract/install/run ... Confirmed locally by substituting a wrong GITLEAKS_SHA256 against this same downloaded archive: the pipe exits 1 at this line, before `tar` ever touches it' — worktree .github/workflows/ci.yml:102-107) describing a manual, one-time demonstration of the checksum-mismatch path. No test or check script was added alongside it, and the builder marked the finding 'unreproduced' (built-3-2.json) rather than adding one. This is the exact pattern this repo's own CLAUDE.md names and prohibits: 'Never describe a one-time manual check as if it were a standing guard ... if no test asserts it, say the check was manual and unguarded, or write the test. A work order that records proofs the tree does not contain is worse than one that records nothing.' The comment now tells every future reader of ci.yml that the mismatch-fails-the-step behavior is 'confirmed,' with nothing in the tree that would catch a future edit (a stray `|| true`, a reordering, a swap to a non-failing check) silently breaking that guarantee. The core gap from the original finding therefore persists in a narrower form: SC-3's checksum-failure behavior and its full-history-scan-comes-back-clean behavior are still exercised by nothing in the diff or on main — only by manual runs that are not recorded as journal 'verified' entries and not committed as scripts, one of which is now asserted as settled fact in a permanent source comment.
